'''Lalji Singh''' (5 July 1947 – 10 December 2017)<ref name="Obit">{{cite news|last1=Dikshit|first1=Rajeev|title=Father of DNA fingerprints Prof Lalji Singh passes away|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/father-of-dna-fingerprints-prof-lalji-singh-passes-away/articleshow/62012808.cms|newspaper=Times of India|date=10 December 2017 |access-date=10 December 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211194712/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/father-of-dna-fingerprints-prof-lalji-singh-passes-away/articleshow/62012808.cms|archive-date=11 December 2017}}</ref> was an Indian scientist who worked in the field of [[DNA profiling|DNA fingerprinting technology]] in India and pioneer of [[Assisted reproductive technology]], where he was popularly known as the "Father of Indian DNA fingerprinting".<ref>{{cite news|title=Lalji Singh, 'father of DNA fingerprinting in India,' passes away|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/lalji-singh-father-of-dna-fingerprinting-in-india-passes-away/article61846771.ece|work=The Hindu|agency=PTI|date=11 December 2017|language=en-IN|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321152655/http://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/lalji-singh-father-of-dna-fingerprinting-in-india-passes-away/article21389954.ece|archive-date=21 March 2018}}</ref> Singh also worked in the areas of [[Sex-determination system|molecular basis of sex determination]], [[Conservation biology|wildlife conservation]] forensics and [[Recent African origin of modern humans|evolution and migration of humans]]. In 2004, he received the [[Padma Shri]] in recognition of his contribution to Indian science and technology.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web|url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |title=Padma Awards |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India |date=2015 |access-date=21 July 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2015 }}</ref>

Singh founded various institutes and laboratories in India, including the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]] in 1995, Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species (LaCONES) in 1998, and Genome Foundation in 2004, aiming to diagnose and treat genetic disorders affecting the Indian population, in particular the under-privileged people residing in rural India.

Singh served as the 25th [[Vice-Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University|Vice Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University]] ([[BHU]]) and Chairman of Board of Governors of [[Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi]] from August 2011 to August 2014. Before his term as Vice Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University, he also served as director of the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]] (CCMB) from May 1998 to July 2009 and Officer on Special Duty (OSD) of [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]] (CDFD), Hyderabad, India in 1995–1999.

== Early life and education ==

Lalji Singh was born and raised in a small village Kalwari in [[Jaunpur district|Jaunpur]] District of [[Uttar Pradesh]], India. His father, Suryanarayan Singh, was a farmer and used to serve as [[Sarpanch|head of the village]]. Singh underwent his primary education up to eighth standard at a government school in Kalwari. However, as there were no further education facilities in the village for senior classes, he was admitted at another school in the nearby village of Pratapganj {{convert|6|-|7|km|mi|abbr=on}} from his village. After completing his 12th standard in the science group at school, he attended [[Banaras Hindu University]] to pursue his graduation in [[Zoology]] and [[cytogenetics]].<ref name="BioSpectrum">{{cite news|last1=Vaidya|first1=Manasi T.|last2=Singh|first2=Nandita|title=The Game Changer Geneticist|url=http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/155909/the-game-changer-geneticist|access-date=16 December 2014|publisher=[[BioSpectrum]]|date=9 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119065624/http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/155909/the-game-changer-geneticist|archive-date=19 January 2015}}</ref>

== University education ==

[[File:Lalji Singh in 1968 at BHU Varanasi India.jpg|thumb|Lalji Singh (second from right) in 1968 at BHU, Varanasi, India]]
Singh obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] degree in 1964 from the [[Banaras Hindu University]] (BHU). Singh scored the highest marks in his [[Master's degree]] class at BHU in 1966, and won the Banaras Hindu Gold Medal for standing first in order of merit. He was awarded a Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) by the [[University Grants Commission (India)]] in 1966. Singh then worked on his doctoral research at the Banaras Hindu University receiving a degree in 1971, for his work on "Evolution of karyotypes in snakes" in the area of cytogenetics under the guidance of professor S.P. Ray Chaudhuri.<ref name="insaprofile">{{cite web|title=Lalji Singh: Fellow of Indian National Science Academy|url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N94-1162|publisher=[[Indian National Science Academy]]|access-date=16 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211073359/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N94-1162|archive-date=11 February 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> A summary of the findings from his doctoral research was published in ''Chromosoma''.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=Lalji|title=Evolution of karyotypes in snakes|journal=Chromosoma|date=1972|volume=38|issue=2|pages=185–236|doi=10.1007/BF00326193|pmid=5066447|s2cid=21621814 }}</ref> Singh received the [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] Medal for Young Scientists in 1974, for his research work in the field of cytogenetics.<ref name="insaprofile" />

== Research career ==

In 1971–72, Singh worked as a research associate at the Department of Zoology, [[University of Calcutta]], and in April 1974, he was appointed as pool officer of [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]]. In 1974, Singh received the [[Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan|Commonwealth Fellowship]] to carry out research at the [[University of Edinburgh]], UK, where he worked until 1987.<ref name="biography">{{cite web|title=Professor (Dr) Lalji Singh – A Profile|url=http://www.ccmb.res.in/staff/lalji/|publisher=[[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150530013958/http://www.ccmb.res.in/staff/lalji/|archive-date=30 May 2015}}</ref> During that time, Singh also worked as a guest scientist at the University of Calcutta, India, for a short period of time and visited the [[Australian National University]] in Canberra as a visiting fellow.<ref name="profilebhu">{{cite web|title=Dr. Lalji Singh: Brief Profile|url=http://www.bhu.ac.in/aboutbhu/administration.html|publisher=[[Banaras Hindu University]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204000112/http://bhu.ac.in/aboutbhu/administration.html|archive-date=4 December 2013}}</ref>

In June 1987, Singh returned to India and joined the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]] (CCMB) in Hyderabad, as a senior scientist. Singh developed and established the DNA fingerprinting technology for forensic investigation of crime and civil disputes.<ref name="biography" /> In July 1998, Singh became the fourth director of the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology|CCMB]], where he served until July 2009.<ref name="ccmbdirlist">{{cite web|title=Past Directors of CCMB|url=http://www.ccmb.res.in/index.php?view=pastdirectors&mid=100&id=25|publisher=[[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology|CCMB]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213071101/http://www.ccmb.res.in/index.php?view=pastdirectors&mid=100&id=25|archive-date=13 December 2014}}</ref> During April 2006 to July 2015, Singh was awarded the J. C. Bose National Research Fellowship of India. He was also awarded the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Fellowship of [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] in January 2010 to December 2014.<ref name="BioSpectrum" /> On 22 August 2009, Singh was appointed as the 25th Vice Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi, India.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rajeev|first1=M.|title=Lalji Singh appointed as BHU Vice-Chancellor|url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/education/college-and-university/lalji-singh-appointed-as-bhu-vicechancellor/article2370000.ece|access-date=16 December 2014|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=19 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321152655/http://www.thehindu.com/features/education/college-and-university/lalji-singh-appointed-as-bhu-vicechancellor/article2370000.ece|archive-date=21 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Padma Shri Lalji Singh is new BHU V-C|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/padma-shri-lalji-singh-is-new-bhu-vc/835220/|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Indian Express]]|date=22 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321152655/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/padma-shri-lalji-singh-is-new-bhu-vc/835220/|archive-date=21 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=PTI|title=BHU's Vice Chancellor Lalji Singh retires|url=http://www.indiatvnews.com/news/india/bhu-vice-chancellor-lalji-singh-retires--40815.html|access-date=16 December 2014|website=www.indiatvnews.com|publisher=Independent News Service|date=23 August 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120123238/http://www.indiatvnews.com/news/india/bhu-vice-chancellor-lalji-singh-retires--40815.html|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Tripathi takes charge as BHU V-C|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/tripathi-takes-charge-as-bhu-v-c/|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Indian Express]]|date=28 November 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207135745/http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/tripathi-takes-charge-as-bhu-v-c/|archive-date=7 December 2014}}</ref> During his three-year tenure as vice chancellor at [[Banaras Hindu University|BHU]], Singh took a {{INR}} 1 token salary from the university.<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Dr Lalji Singh to take only Re 1 as wage for BHU VC|url=http://news.webindia123.com/news/articles/india/20110804/1805467.html|access-date=16 December 2014|website=WebIndia123|date=4 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120152205/http://news.webindia123.com/news/articles/india/20110804/1805467.html|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Dr Lalji Singh to take only Re 1 as wage for Banaras Hindu University – Vice Chancellor|url=http://www.itbhuglobal.org/chronicle/archives/2011/08/dr_lalji_singh.php|access-date=15 January 2015|publisher=IIT-BHU Chronicle|date=21 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150627070919/http://www.itbhuglobal.org/chronicle/archives/2011/08/dr_lalji_singh.php|archive-date=27 June 2015}}</ref>

From 2014 Singh was associated with several academic and research organisations in various capacities. These included being a member of the Governing Board of [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]] (ICAR), New Delhi; chairman of the Research Advisory Council (RAC) of National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR), Karnal; chairman of the RAC of Project Directorate on Poultry (PDP), Hyderabad; member of the advisory committee of Pharmacopeia Commission of India; chairman of the RAC of National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Lucknow; member of the Board of Management of Sri Ramachandra University, Chennai and member of the Board of Governors of [[Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research]] (IISER) Mohali.<ref name="profilebhu" /> Singh also served as director of the Genome Foundation, a non-profit organization aiming to develop cheap molecular diagnostics for genetic disorders prevalent in rural India.<ref name="genomefoundation">{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=Genome Foundation to set up centres in rural areas|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/Genome-Foundation-to-set-up-centres-in-rural-areas/articleshow/8766639.cms|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=8 June 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103200252/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/Genome-Foundation-to-set-up-centres-in-rural-areas/articleshow/8766639.cms|archive-date=3 January 2017}}</ref>

Singh published more than 230 research papers during his 45 years of research, and {{as of|April 2013|lc=y}} he had an [[h-index]] of 30.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mukherjee|first1=Bhaskar|title=A scientometric profile of Prof. Lalji Singh as seen through Web of Science and Scopus|journal=Annals of Library and Information Studies|date=September 2013|volume=60|pages=195–203|url=http://nopr.niscair.res.in/bitstream/123456789/22891/1/ALIS%2060%283%29%20195-203.pdf|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211065815/http://nopr.niscair.res.in/bitstream/123456789/22891/1/ALIS%2060%283%29%20195-203.pdf|archive-date=11 February 2015}}</ref>

== Innovations and contributions to science and technology ==

=== DNA fingerprinting technology ===

During his early science career as a Masters student in 1968, Singh became interested in studying the cytogenetics of Indian snakes.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Singh|first1=Binay|title=Charm of snakes led this scientist to DNA fingerprinting|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/Charm-of-snakes-led-this-scientist-to-DNA-fingerprinting/articleshow/15162804.cms|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=26 July 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120727065645/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/Charm-of-snakes-led-this-scientist-to-DNA-fingerprinting/articleshow/15162804.cms|archive-date=27 July 2012}}</ref> During the 1970s, while studying the evolution of [[Allosome|sex chromosome]] in a species of an Indian snake, the [[banded krait]], Singh and his colleagues identified a highly conserved repeated DNA sequences in the banded krait and other vertebrates,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Sharma|first2=T.|last3=Ray-Chaudhuri|first3=S.P.|title=Multiple sex chromosomes in the common krait, Bungarus caeruleus Schneider|journal=Chromosoma|year=1970|volume=31|issue=4|pages=386–391|pmid=5490305|doi=10.1007/bf00285830|s2cid=30146980 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Purdom|first2=I.F.|last3=Jones|first3=K.W.|title=The chromosomal localization of satellite DNA in Ptyas mucosus (Ophidia, Colubridae)|journal=Chromosoma|year=1976|volume=57|issue=2|pages=177–184|doi=10.1007/BF00292916|pmid=954552|s2cid=1315709 }}</ref> which they named the "Banded Krait Minor" (Bkm) sequences in 1980.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Purdom|first2=I.F.|last3=Jones|first3=K.W.|title=Sex chromosome associated satellite DNA: Evolution and conservation|journal=Chromosoma|year=1980|volume=79|issue=2|pages=137–157|pmid=7398495|doi=10.1007/bf01175181|s2cid=19592537 }}</ref> These Bkm sequences were conserved across various species and were found to be polymorphic in humans.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Jones|first2=K.W.|title=Bkm sequences are polymorphic in humans and are clustered in pericentric regions of various acrocentric chromosomes including the Y|journal=Human Genetics|year=1986|volume=73|issue=4|pages=304–308|pmid=3017839|doi=10.1007/bf00279091|s2cid=12349826 }}</ref>
In 1987 through 1988, while working in the [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology|CCMB]], Singh established that this Bkm-derived probe could be used to generate individual specific DNA Fingerprints of humans for forensic investigations; and in 1988, he used that probe for the first time to solve a case of parentage dispute in India.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jayaraman|first1=K.S.|title=Cut-price fingerprints.|journal=Nature|year=1989|volume=340|issue=6230|page=175|pmid=2755472|doi=10.1038/340175c0|bibcode=1989Natur.340..175J|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 1991, Singh produced the first DNA fingerprinting based evidence in an Indian Court to settle a disputed paternity.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kunhiraman vs Manoj on 27 February, 1991 [II (1991) DMC 499]|url=http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115193/|website=www.indiankanoon.org|publisher=[[Kerala High Court]]|access-date=17 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120114240/http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115193/|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=Lalji|title=DNA profiling and its application|journal=Current Science|date=1991|volume=60|pages=580–585}}</ref> This was followed by DNA fingerprinting based resolution of hundreds of civil and criminal cases, including cases such as the assassination case(s) of [[Beant Singh (chief minister)|Beant Singh]] and [[Rajiv Gandhi]],<ref name="Madras High Court">{{cite web|title=Chandradevi (A-3) vs State Of Tamil Nadu on 12 December, 2002|url=http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12253/?type=print|website=www.indiankanoon.org|publisher=[[Madras High Court]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120115212/http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12253/?type=print|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> [[Naina Sahni]] Tandoor murder case,<ref>{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=Nailing a criminal the DNA way|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/Nailing-a-criminal-the-DNA-way/articleshow/381928383.cms|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=21 August 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170104011418/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/Nailing-a-criminal-the-DNA-way/articleshow/381928383.cms|archive-date=4 January 2017}}</ref> [[Swami Premananda (guru)|Swami Premananda]] case,<ref name="Madras High Court"/><ref>{{cite web|title=TWO ASPECTS OF SWAMI PREMANANDA: "THE AVATAR OF THIS AGE" plus CONVICTED RAPIST & MURDERER|url=http://www.exbaba.com/shortnews/gurugallery/premananda.htm|website=www.exbaba.com|access-date=16 December 2014}}</ref> Swami Shraddhananda case,<ref>{{cite web|title=Criminal Appeal No. 454 of 2006, Swamy Shraddananda @ Murali Manohar Mishra vs State Of Karnataka, the Supreme Court of India, decided on 22 July 2008|url=http://indiankanoon.org/doc/989335/|website=www.indiankanoon.org|publisher=[[Supreme Court of India]]|access-date=24 January 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211065419/http://indiankanoon.org/doc/989335/|archive-date=11 February 2015}}</ref> and [[Priyadarshini Mattoo]] murder case.<ref>{{cite web|title=Santosh Kumar Singh vs State Th. Cbi on 6 October, 2010|url=http://indiankanoon.org/doc/760449/|website=www.indiankanoon.org|publisher=[[Supreme Court of India]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120122344/http://indiankanoon.org/doc/760449/|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref>

This established the DNA fingerprinting to be used as evidence in the legal system of India.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rajagopal|first1=Krishnadas|title=SC pulls up trial court for not taking DNA experts seriously|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/sc-pulls-up-trial-court-for-not-taking-dna-experts-seriously/693714/|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Indian Express]]|date=7 October 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321152655/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/sc-pulls-up-trial-court-for-not-taking-dna-experts-seriously/693714/|archive-date=21 March 2018}}</ref> Singh's work in this arena prompted the government of India's [[Department of Biotechnology]] to form an autonomous institution, the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics|Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD)]] in 1995, with the aim to provide DNA fingerprinting services to the country, especially for human identification purposes.<ref name="profilebhu" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Official website of Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD)|url=http://www.cdfd.org.in/|access-date=17 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218155618/http://cdfd.org.in/|archive-date=18 December 2014}}</ref>

Singh's lifetime contributions for the development and establishment of indigenous [[DNA profiling|DNA Fingerprinting Technology]] in India were recognized and he has been called the "Father of DNA fingerprinting" in India.<ref>{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=BHU introduces PG course in forensic science from this session|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/BHU-introduces-PG-course-in-forensic-science-from-this-session/articleshow/37765555.cms|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=4 July 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708143912/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/varanasi/BHU-introduces-PG-course-in-forensic-science-from-this-session/articleshow/37765555.cms|archive-date=8 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=DNA inventor Dr Lalji Singh gets Nayudamma Award|url=http://www.telugumirchi.com/en/other-news/dna-inventor-dr-lalji-singh-gets-nayudamma-award.html|access-date=16 December 2014|website=Telugu Mirchi|date=3 February 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120145347/http://www.telugumirchi.com/en/other-news/dna-inventor-dr-lalji-singh-gets-nayudamma-award.html|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=Forensic top expert visiting Allahabad for lecture|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/allahabad/Forensic-top-expert-visiting-Allahabad-for-lecture/articleshow/17175059.cms|access-date=22 January 2015|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=11 November 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923170555/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/allahabad/Forensic-top-expert-visiting-Allahabad-for-lecture/articleshow/17175059.cms|archive-date=23 September 2016}}</ref>

=== Wildlife conservation and forensics ===
[[File:Spottted Deer LaCONES.jpg|thumb|A spotted deer fawn born out of first successful artificial insemination in India at LaCONES on 14 March 2006]]
While serving as director of [[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology|CCMB]], Singh realized an urgent need for assessment and conservation of the wildlife resources of India. To address that need, he conceptualized the [[Laboratory for conservation of endangered species]] (LaCONES) in 1998.<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=President to open LaCONES|url=http://www.oneindia.com/2006/11/20/president-to-open-lacones-1164028176.html|access-date=17 December 2014|publisher=[[Oneindia.com]]|date=20 November 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120130642/http://www.oneindia.com/2006/11/20/president-to-open-lacones-1164028176.html|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> The foundation stone of this laboratory was laid by the Minister of Environment and Forests, [[Government of India]] on 16 September 2001. On 2 February 2007, the laboratory was inaugurated and dedicated to the nation by then President of India [[A. P. J. Abdul Kalam|A.P.J. Abdul Kalam]].<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=PRESIDENT 'S ADDRESS AT THE DEDICATION OF THE LABORATORY FOR THE CONSERVATION OF ENDANGERED SPECIES (LACONES), HYDERABAD|url=http://pib.nic.in/release/rel_print_page1.asp?relid=24554|access-date=17 December 2014|publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]], Government of India|date=1 February 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120133629/http://pib.nic.in/release/rel_print_page1.asp?relid=24554|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=President dedicates LaCONES to nation|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-economy/president-dedicates-lacones-to-nation/article1648332.ece|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[Business Line|The Hindu: Business Line]]|date=3 February 2007}}</ref>

LaCONES serves as a research laboratory for the conservation and preservation of wildlife resources using advanced technological interventions;<ref>{{cite web|title=Virtual Tour of LaCONES|url=http://ccmb.res.in/vr/ccmb-vr-flash/lacones-vr/index.html|publisher=[[Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology|CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology]]|access-date=19 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220031337/http://ccmb.res.in/vr/ccmb-vr-flash/lacones-vr/index.html|archive-date=20 December 2014}}</ref> and also the "National Wildlife Forensic Cell" to provide wildlife identification services for the nation, based on the fundamental discovery of universal primer technology made by [[Sunil Kumar Verma]] and Singh (2001).<ref name="AutoZ3-1">{{cite web|last1=Verma|first1=Sunil Kumar|last2=Singh|first2=Lalji|title=US Patent No 7141364: Verma and Singh 2001|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&co1=AND&d=PTXT&s1=7141364&OS=7141364&RS=7141364|publisher=[[United States Patent and Trademark Office]]|access-date=29 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402115849/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&co1=AND&d=PTXT&s1=7141364&OS=7141364&RS=7141364|archive-date=2 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Singh|first1=Lalit T.|title=It's only a leopard: lab finding|url=http://www.thehindu.com/2002/02/10/stories/2002021003090500.htm|access-date=29 December 2014|website=[[The Hindu]]|date=10 February 2002|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303193400/http://www.thehindu.com/2002/02/10/stories/2002021003090500.htm|archive-date=3 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=CCMB develops DNA test to identify animal species|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2003/04/30/stories/2003043001921900.htm|website=[[Business Line|The Hindu: Business Line]]|date=30 April 2003|access-date=18 November 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031121103000/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2003/04/30/stories/2003043001921900.htm|archive-date=21 November 2003}}</ref> The first DNA-based test for establishing the species identity of an unknown biological sample pertaining to a case of wildlife crime, was conducted in that laboratory in 2000.<ref>{{cite web|title=Verma and Singh, Universal Primer technology US and PCT Patent application No: PCT/IN01/00055, First Filling Date: 28/03/2001; Priority date: 28/03/2001|url=http://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/WO2002077278|access-date=19 December 2014|publisher=[[World Intellectual Property Organization]]|date=3 October 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120140849/http://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/WO2002077278|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> Since then, the laboratory has undertaken thousands of such cases on a routine basis for the entire country and has revitalized the field of wildlife forensics.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSIR-Centre for Cellular & Molecular Biology (CSIR-CCMB) had developed DNA barcoding technology|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=108185|agency=[[Press Information Bureau]], Ministry of Science & Technology, [[Government of India]]|date=6 August 2014|access-date=18 November 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225163128/http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=108185|archive-date=25 December 2014}}<!-- press release? --></ref>

The laboratory recorded a major success in the [[Assisted reproductive technology]] (ART) of wild animals, when the world's first successful [[artificial insemination]] of an in estrus induced [[Chital|spotted deer]], by non-surgical intra-vaginal insemination done in the laboratory, led to the birth of a live fawn on 14 March 2006.<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=CCMB's non-invasive artificial insemination bears fawn|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/ccmb-s-non-invasive-artificial-insemination-bears-fawn-106032901002_1.html|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[Business Standard]]|date=29 March 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120140926/http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/ccmb-s-non-invasive-artificial-insemination-bears-fawn-106032901002_1.html|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=CCMB scientists spawn spotted fawn|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/CCMB-scientists-spawn-spotted-fawn/articleshow/1468243.cms|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=29 March 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170102195158/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/CCMB-scientists-spawn-spotted-fawn/articleshow/1468243.cms|archive-date=2 January 2017}}</ref> This achievement was further followed by an [[artificial insemination]] (AI) assisted birth of an Indian [[blackbuck]] fawn in August 2007. These were the first reports in the world of such successful [[Artificial insemination|AI]] of wild animals.<ref>{{cite web|title=LaCONES delivers "BLACKY", a Black Buck|url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/Blacky-CCMB.pdf|publisher=[[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR)|access-date=19 December 2014|date=24 August 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120124920/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/Blacky-CCMB.pdf|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref>

On the World Heritage Day in 2013, the LaCONES campus was recognized as a "Heritage Monument" by the Indian National Trust for Art and Culture (Intach)<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Hyderabad monuments awarded|url=http://archives.deccanchronicle.com/130419/news-current-affairs/article/hyderabad-monuments-awarded|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[Deccan Chronicle]]|date=19 April 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002082150/http://archives.deccanchronicle.com/130419/news-current-affairs/article/hyderabad-monuments-awarded|archive-date=2 October 2015}}</ref> for its notable architecture and design.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Corradi|first1=Mara|title=Shirish Beri: Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species|url=http://www.floornature.com/projects-commerce/project-shirish-beri-laboratory-for-the-conservation-of-endangered-species-9131/|access-date=17 December 2014|publisher=Floornature|date=29 January 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120143854/http://www.floornature.com/projects-commerce/project-shirish-beri-laboratory-for-the-conservation-of-endangered-species-9131/|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Beri|first1=Shirish|last2=and Associates|title=LaCONES (Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species)|url=http://www.architecture-page.com/go/projects/lacones-laboratory-conservation-endangered-species__all|publisher=Architecture-page|access-date=17 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120134817/http://www.architecture-page.com/go/projects/lacones-laboratory-conservation-endangered-species__all|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref>

=== Molecular basis of sex determination ===
In 1982, Singh and his colleagues discovered that a tiny portion of the short arm of sex-determining [[Y chromosome]] was necessary and sufficient to convert a female mouse to male.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Jones|first2=K.W.|title=Sex reversal in the mouse (Mus musculus) is caused by a recurrent nonreciprocal crossover involving the X and an aberrant Y chromosome|journal=Cell|date=1982|volume=28|issue=2|pages=205–216|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(82)90338-5|pmid=7060127|s2cid=20454958 |url=http://www.cell.com/cell/pdf/0092-8674%2882%2990338-5.pdf}}</ref> This fundamental discovery provided a new concept of [[Chromosomal translocation]] of sex-determining region from Y chromosome to [[X chromosome]]s causing [[sex reversal]] in mice. These findings later became the foundation for the discovery of a similar phenomenon of [[Sex reversal|sex reversal in humans]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Guellaen|first1=Georges|last2=Casanova|first2=Myriam|last3=Bishop|first3=Colin|last4=Geldwerth|first4=Danielle|last5= Andre|first5=Gabriel|last6=Fellous|first6=Marc|last7= Weissenbach|first7=Jean|title=Human XX males with Y single-copy DNA fragments|journal=Nature|date=1984|volume=307|issue=5947|pages=172–173|doi=10.1038/307172a0|pmid=6537828|bibcode=1984Natur.307..172G|s2cid=1072978 }}<!--|access-date=21 January 2015--></ref>

=== DNA-based molecular diagnostics ===
Until 1998, India did not have an adequate facility for diagnosis of [[genetic disorder]]s, prevalent in the country. The fundamental research carried out by Singh and his colleagues in that area, led to conceptualization and establishment of the first DNA based diagnostic laboratory in the country.<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Genetic fingerprinting catches on|url=http://www.indiaenvironmentportal.org.in/content/4381/genetic-fingerprinting-catches-on/|access-date=17 December 2014|publisher=[[Centre for Science and Environment]]|date=30 October 1992|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120142400/http://www.indiaenvironmentportal.org.in/content/4381/genetic-fingerprinting-catches-on/|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> The lab later evolved into a separate institute, the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]] in Hyderabad, India to provide advanced DNA based molecular diagnostics services for the nation.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Somasekhar|first1=M.|title=DNA fingerprinting comes of age|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/opinion/dna-fingerprinting-comes-of-age/article3746620.ece|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[Business Line|The Hindu: Business Line]]|date=9 August 2012}}</ref>

=== Novel insights into evolution and migration of humans ===
The fundamental DNA-based research carried out by Singh and his colleagues on [[Indigenous peoples|primitive tribes]] including the tribal population of the [[Andaman and Nicobar Islands]], provided critical insights into the evolution and migration of humans, suggesting the out of Africa route of modern humans about 60,000 years ago to the [[Andaman Islands]].<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=DNA polymorphism provides insight into human origin|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/ldquoDNA-polymorphism-provides-insight-into-human-originrdquo/article14932836.ece|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Hindu]]|date=4 March 2011}}</ref> These findings have furthered the scientific community's understanding of the [[Anthropogeny|origin of man]] in terms of evolution and migration from place to place.<ref>{{cite news|last1=TNN|title=Aryan-Dravidian divide a myth: Study|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Aryan-Dravidian-divide-a-myth-Study/articleshow/5053274.cms|access-date=16 December 2014|website=[[The Times of India]]|date=25 September 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108193900/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Aryan-Dravidian-divide-a-myth-Study/articleshow/5053274.cms|archive-date=8 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chellappan|first1=Kumar|title=New research debunks Aryan invasion theory|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-new-research-debunks-aryan-invasion-theory-1623744|website=[[Daily News and Analysis]]|access-date=16 December 2014|date=10 December 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222190645/http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-new-research-debunks-aryan-invasion-theory-1623744|archive-date=22 December 2014}}</ref>

=== Genome Foundation ===
In 2004, Singh founded a non-profit research and service organization, the Genome Foundation, with the aim of diagnosing and treating [[genetic disorder]] affecting the Indian population, in particular the under-privileged people residing in rural India, with the participation and voluntary services of scientists and professionals.<ref name="genomefoundation" /><ref>{{cite news|last1=Singh|first1=Lalit T.|title=Even a rupee can help fund its cause|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/even-a-rupee-can-help-fund-its-cause/article6686461.ece|access-date=17 December 2014|website=[[The Hindu]]|date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

==Death==
Lalji Singh died in [[Varanasi]], India following a heart attack on 10 December 2017 at the age of 70. He complained of chest pain when he reached the [[Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport]] to board a flight for [[Delhi]]. He was taken to the [[Sir Sunderlal Hospital|Banaras Hindu University (BHU) Trauma Centre]] from there but he could not be saved.<ref name="Obit"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/lalji-singh-father-of-dna-fingerprinting-in-india-passes-away/article61846771.ece|title=Lalji Singh, 'father of DNA fingerprinting in India,' passes away|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=11 December 2017|date=11 December 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321152655/http://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/lalji-singh-father-of-dna-fingerprinting-in-india-passes-away/article21389954.ece|archive-date=21 March 2018}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Singh holds fellowships from several Indian and Foreign academies. These include:
* Fellow of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (FASc), (elected in 1989)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of [[The National Academy of Sciences, India]] (FNASc), (elected in 1991)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of [[Indian National Science Academy]] (FNA) (elected in 1993)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of Andhra Pradesh Akademi of Sciences (elected in 2000)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]] (FAAS) (elected in 2001)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of [[National Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FAMS) (elected in 2002)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Fellow of [[TWAS|Third World Academy of Sciences]] (FTWAS) (elected in 2002)<ref>{{cite web|title=Lalji Singh: Fellow of TWAS|url=http://twas.org/member/singh-lalji|website=www.twas.org|publisher=[[TWAS|The World Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=17 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002053211/http://twas.org/member/singh-lalji|archive-date=2 October 2015}}</ref>

Some of the notable awards conferred to Singh are as follows:
* [[Indian National Science Academy]] Medal for Young Scientists, (1974)<ref name="insaprofile" />
* [[Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan|Commonwealth Fellowship]], (1974–1976)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] Technology Award (Twice: 1992 and 2008; The 2008 Award was jointly conferred to [[Sunil Kumar Verma|Verma]] and Singh),<ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=CSIR award for CCMB|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-andhrapradesh/CSIR-award-for-CCMB/article15309677.ece|access-date=18 November 2014|website=[[The Hindu]]|date=24 September 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=CCMB bags CSIR technology award for life sciences 2008|url=http://news.webindia123.com/news/articles/India/20080923/1060944.html|access-date=18 November 2014|publisher=WebIndia123|date=23 September 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227064346/http://news.webindia123.com/news/articles/India/20080923/1060944.html|archive-date=27 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=CSIR Technology Awards – 2008|url=http://dst.gov.in/whats_new/press-release08/csir-awards-2008.htm|access-date=18 November 2014|publisher=[[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], [[Government of India]]|date=26 September 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221162249/http://dst.gov.in/whats_new/press-release08/csir-awards-2008.htm|archive-date=21 December 2014}}<!-- press release? --></ref>
* [[Ranbaxy Laboratories|Ranbaxy]] research Award (1994)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Goyal Prize in Life Sciences (2000)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* Vigyan Gaurav Award (2003)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* [[FICCI]] Award (2002–03)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* The New Millennium Plaques of Honour, (2002), for services in the field of biological sciences from the Prime Minister of India at the 89th Session of the [[Indian Science Congress Association|Indian Science Congress]].<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* JC Bos National Fellowship (2006)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] Bhatnagar Fellowship (2009)<ref name="biography" /><ref name="profilebhu" />
* [[National Research Development Corporation|NRDC]] Meritorious Invention Award (2009), jointly conferred to [[Sunil Kumar Verma|Verma]] and Singh),<ref>{{cite web|title=NRDC Awards 2009|url=http://www.nrdcindia.com/english/index.php/awards/awarded-inventions-awarded-inventions/24-1991|access-date=31 December 2014|publisher=[[National Research Development Corporation]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221170158/http://www.nrdcindia.com/english/index.php/awards/awarded-inventions-awarded-inventions/24-1991|archive-date=21 December 2014}}</ref>
* Biospectrum Life Time Achievement Award (2011).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Kelath|first1=Uma|title=BioSpectrum awards excellence|url=http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/155570/biospectrum-awards-excellence|publisher=Biospectrum|access-date=17 December 2014|date=9 January 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119193612/http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/news/155570/biospectrum-awards-excellence|archive-date=19 January 2015}}</ref>
* The [[Padma Shri]], (2004), in recognition of his contributions to Indian science and technology.<ref name="padmaaward">{{cite web|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|title=Padma Shri Awardees – 2004|url=http://archive.india.gov.in/myindia/padmashri_awards_list1.php?start=610|publisher=[[Government of India]]|access-date=16 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120163854/http://archive.india.gov.in/myindia/padmashri_awards_list1.php?start=610|archive-date=20 January 2015}}</ref>

Singh has also been awarded "Honorary D.Sc. degree" by six Universities including the [[Banaras Hindu University]].<ref name="profilebhu" />

== Selected publications ==
* Chromosomes and classification of the snakes of the family Boidae<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Singh|first1=L.|last2=Sharma|first2=T.|last3=Ray-Chaudhuri|first3=S.P.|year=1968|title=Chromosomes and classification of the snakes of the family Boidae|url=https://doc-04-as-docs.googleusercontent.com/docs/securesc/ha0ro937gcuc7l7deffksulhg5h7mbp1/rqrnv565t11aaou98nj7u2v962ho9kdk/1416326400000/03715982868602056797/*/0B3-s774vYQRac2F6cmxncHA1MTQ?e=view|journal=Cytogenetics|volume=7|issue=3|pages=161–168|doi=10.1159/000129980|pmid=5693182|url-access=subscription}}{{Dead link|date=August 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
